messages:
Sam (community): hey team, got a support case — user followed the Ruby quickstart and their long-lived streaming job started getting 401s after ~30m. they pasted the snippet from docs exactly.
Alice K: uuuh. thanks for the report. which quickstart URL?
Sam (community): https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart/ruby (they included the snippet inline). says use API_KEY directly in client config.
Ben T: that's our minimal example on purpose to keep copy tiny. but it does cause problems for refreshable token setups, especially with on-prem KMS rotation.
Carmen R: can we make the snippet show a refreshable token pattern instead of raw key? even a short lambda would help.
Alice K: agreed. the issue multiplies when folks use streaming + single client instance. the Ruby SDK currently caches the header and doesn't call the token provider between reconnects in some flow.
Ben T: i dug in — the client will call the token provider on init and on reconnect, but there are cases (keepalive with chunked stream) where the auth header isn't re-evaluated. that's our bug.
Sam (community): user had a rotating token from their infra; once token rotated, existing streams tried to use old token and got 401, then our retry logic gave up after a single immediate retry.
Alice K: two fixes: docs change to recommend a refreshable token hook for sample apps + small SDK patch to ensure provider is consulted before each stream handshake and to add exponential backoff on 401 for stream connect.
Carmen R: happy to update quickstart. proposal for snippet:
```ruby
# minimal refreshable token example
client = Redwood::Client.new(default_headers: lambda { { 'Authorization' => "Bearer #{ENV['REDWOOD_REFRESHABLE_TOKEN']()}" } })
# streaming usage
client.chat.stream do |chunk|
  puts chunk.text
end
```
Ben T: we don't actually support a lambda for default_headers yet in the public gem API. i can add it but want tests.
Alice K: can we ship docs first with a small note: "for long-lived jobs use a rotating token provider; see ruby SDK docs for sample code" and link to a follow-up PR for the SDK change? ship fast.
Ben T: i'll open the SDK PR now and include unit + integration test that simulates token rotation during streaming connect. also fix retry behavior on 401s (simple exp backoff with jitter).
Ben T: created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/4623 — includes implementation + tests. cc @Alice K @Carmen R
docs-bot: PR 4623 linked in docs checklist.
Carmen R: thanks. i'll update quickstart to point to the PR for the example until we release a gem that contains the lambda support. will add an inline callout so community won't copy the insecure pattern.
Sam (community): awesome. can we add a small note for on-prem/private customers about KMS token rotation patterns? they were really confused and opened a support ticket.
Alice K: yes. Carmen, add a brief KMS note and link to the private deployment section.
Ben T: heads up — CI flake popped in ruby-integration tests on 2.7 matrix while running the new tests, looks like timezone-sensitive timestamp in a fixture. i'll push a fix.
build-bot: build failing on ruby-sdk/integration (2.7) — job 8791.
Ben T: pushed fix for tz fixture, CI rerun queued: https://ci.redwood.ai/8791
Alice K: once CI is green, can we draft a short incident/annouce in #announcements describing change? want to highlight guidance and link to PRs so users know what to do.
Carmen R: yep. i'll also add a tiny migration note in the changelog for the next release.
Sam (community): thanks everyone — user confirmed workaround (manual token rotation + restart) works for now, but they'll wait for the gem patch. :thumbsup:
Ben T: ETA for release with fix: hotpatch release tomorrow, then full release next week.
Alice K: thanks all. follow-ups: Carmen to update quickstart (temp workaround), Ben to land PR & release, docs-bot to surface links.
